assessment: The incumbent supplies inexpensive printed prompts and a predictable conversational routine. Seven frequent attendees value that routine, supporting its retention without establishing causality. A concrete limitation is five occasional attendees finding familiar partners' conversations difficult to enter; predictability may benefit returning learners while leaving entry unsupported. Slow pairing and partner changes are compatible with several explanations, including familiarity, proficiency or preference. Of 72 slips, 49 report sufficient useful practice and 48 identify preparation correctly, below the respective targets among respondents. There were 97 attendances; missing slips, untimed speech and unlinked responses limit conclusions. Coordination sometimes exceeds 90 minutes. All evidence is stipulated synthetic observation.

openings.claim: Prior conversational familiarity may impede entry independently of proficiency; a self-contained opening exchange could preserve the helpful routine while improving access.
openings.delta: Keep the topic and pair practice, but begin with a brief printed exchange requiring no previous attendance, offering optional support prompts and extension questions without public proficiency labels.
openings.prediction: With pairs already formed, the entry exchange increases early speaking participation and reported usefulness among occasional attendees; pairing delays need not change.
openings.probe: Counterbalance ordinary and self-contained openings across comparable rounds. Observe turn distribution anonymously and collect optional anonymous attendance-frequency and usefulness responses. Improvement after pairing would distinguish an entry barrier from pairing delay alone, although proficiency remains a possible moderator.
assumptions: Existing prompts can support both rounds within 75 minutes.
Preparation and observation can fit volunteer capacity; measure their cost.

openings.claim: Ambiguous task currency may contribute to earlier-task answers; explicit session dates could reduce that specific error.
openings.delta: Mark the existing printed sheet with one clearly dated next preparation task and make current copies available at every session, including to returning participants.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task answers decline, especially among print-only users; blank responses may persist if comprehension is the main barrier.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, tally correct, earlier and blank answers separately, optionally identifying print-only use anonymously. Log preparation queries and total coordination time; assess all original success measures rather than task accuracy alone.
assumptions: A next task can be selected before sheets are printed.
Dates are understandable; improvement remains a hypothesis until observed.
